record.paper_title: 20 Open Questions About Deformations of Compactifiable Manifolds
record.original_question: Let X be a pseudoconcave complex space. When does there exist a compact complex space W and an open embedding j: X -> W such that the complement W \ j(X) is very small, for example a finite set?

evidence.quote: Question 14. Let X be a pseudoconcave complex space. When is there a compact complex space W and an open embedding j : X −→ W such that W \ j(X) is “very small”, for instance a finite set?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A reduced complex space $X$ is called pseudoconcave if there exists a relatively compact open subset $Y \Subset X$ such that for every point $x \in \partial Y$ there is a neighborhood $U_x$ of $x$ in $X$ with the property that every holomorphic function on $U_x \cap Y$ extends holomorphically to all of $U_x$ (so that, intuitively, $X$ has a pseudoconcave boundary along which holomorphic functions extend inward). A compactification of $X$ is a compact complex space $W$ together with an open holomorphic embedding $j : X \hookrightarrow W$; the boundary of the compactification is the analytic-set complement $W \setminus j(X)$.

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on a pseudoconcave complex space $X$ under which there exists a compactification $j : X \hookrightarrow W$ into a compact complex space $W$ whose boundary $W \setminus j(X)$ is "very small" — for instance, a finite set of points, or more generally an analytic subset of complex dimension zero.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question about characterizing when pseudoconcave complex spaces admit compactifications with very small (e.g., finite) boundary. No published resolution was located; partial results exist in the literature on Andreotti pseudoconcave spaces and their algebraic dimension/compactifications, but a complete characterization appears not to be known.
